data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all relevant AUR repository files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, calibraw.desktop) and found no malicious behavior. The PKGBUILD is a standard Rust package that downloads from the official GitHub repository with pinned SHA-256 checksums, uses standard cargo build, and installs only the compiled binary and metadata files. No injection patterns, suspicious network operations, or unexpected code execution were identified.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error, not substantive analysis. The qwen model encountered an HTTP 400 BadRequestError during the full PKGBUILD review phase, causing it to return inconclusive. Notably, the qwen model had successfully completed an initial PKGBUILD audit (finding it safe to source), but failed during the comprehensive file review. This is a coverage failure, not a security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to complete PKGBUILD audit due to HTTP 400 API error during full review phase
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should trigger automatic retry logic rather than immediately marking files as inconclusive
When a model successfully completes an initial PKGBUILD audit but fails during full review, the system should preserve and use the initial audit result rather than discarding it
Distinguish between tool failures and substantive security findings in verdict reporting - a tool error should not be conflated with an inconclusive security assessment
